exercise.name: Band Back Extension

reference.title: Band back extension
reference.listing: Animated GIF (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; authored as a standing back extension: band under the feet, held at the front of the shoulders, hinge and stand tall)

equipment: Resistance band (two, or one long band under both feet)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace as you hinge forward, breathe out as you extend back up to standing.

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure or when the back starts to round (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: shorter band or a stronger band for more tension
prescription.progression: Stronger band, longer pause at the bottom, then a dumbbell good morning or a 45-degree back extension

cues.text: Stand on the band with both feet hip width, knees soft. Hold the band ends at the front of the shoulders, elbows down, chest tall.
Breathe in, push the hips back and tip the trunk forward with a long back; the band slackens a little.
Stop when the hamstrings are stretched, trunk well inclined, back still long.
Breathe out and extend back up against the band, hips forward, until you stand tall.
Stand tall, ribs down, then hinge again.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the low back to go lower
mistakes.fix: Stop the hinge where the back stays long.
Hips back, knees only soft, shins nearly vertical.
Finish tall with the ribs down and the glutes squeezed.

mistakes.mistake: Hands drifting away from the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Keep the hands fixed at the shoulders; the trunk does the work.

kinematics.norm: Hinge to a hamstring stretch, as in the good morning (Vigotsky 2015 measured hip and trunk angles in the good morning)
Soft knees, about 10-20 degrees (clinical opinion; Vigotsky 2015)
Close to neutral; a little rounding near the bottom is common, keep it small (clinical opinion)
Fixed at the front of the shoulders (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band back extension, animated GIF (movement reference)
Vigotsky et al. 2015, effects of load on good morning kinematics and EMG activity (PeerJ 3:e708)
McAllister, Hammond, Schilling, Ferreria, Reed & Weiss 2014, muscle activation during various hamstring exercises (J Strength Cond Res 28(6):1573-1580)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the bands before each set and keep them centred under the feet: a band that slips can snap up toward the face.
Keep the back long; stop the hinge before the low back rounds.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: shorter range and more knee bend.
Hamstring tightness: hinge only as far as the back stays long.
progressions: Dumbbell good morning or 45-degree back extension.

muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Prime mover: extend the trunk back to standing and hold the back long through the hinge. In the good morning the erector spinae worked through the range (Vigotsky 2015); the band loads the top more than the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Prime mover: extend the trunk back to standing (Vigotsky 2015).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Extend the hip and lengthen at the bottom of the hinge; hinge exercises load the hamstrings (McAllister 2014; Vigotsky 2015).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Extend the hip and lengthen at the bottom of the hinge (McAllister 2014; Vigotsky 2015).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extend the hip, mostly near the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extend the hip, mostly near the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the ribs stay down at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Hold the hands at the shoulders (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Hold the hands at the shoulders (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Hold the elbows bent against the band (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the elbows bent against the band (clinical opinion).
